title: Chroma-Preserving Token Remap and Interactive State Overrides for Low-Contrast Dark Consoles
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Several console components (dense tables, compact buttons, and inline chart legends) look washed-out or lose brand chroma in our darkest theme when users enable high-contrast or low-brightness displays. Existing token mappings simply invert or desaturate values which causes: color collisions, reduced distinction between interactive states, and chart series that are indistinguishable.

Goal: Produce a token remapping and component override strategy that preserves perceptual chroma and inter-component contrast in deep dark themes while meeting WCAG contrast targets for primary interactive states. The deliverable is a design spec + implementation guidance for engineers and a small set of token transforms that can be applied at runtime (console theming layer).

Scope: tokens (semantic surface/ink/brand shades), component overrides (buttons, dense tables, chart series/legend), interactive states (hover/focus/active/disabled), and a migration plan for existing components. This is a design-first ticket with close engineering collaboration for runtime feasibility (delta blending, HSLuv conversions).
acceptance_criteria: Design spec includes a deterministic token transform algorithm with examples for 6 brand anchors across light and dark extremes.
Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost) maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast for text on background in active/focus states on the darkest surface variants.
Table zebra-striping approach that preserves row separation without reducing chart color legibility in embedded sparklines.
Chart color recommendation table with alternate high-chroma palettes and fallback ordering for 1–8 series; sample Vega-Lite configs included.
Implementation guidance and acceptance tests for engineering: transformation pseudocode, performance considerations, and feature flag rollout plan.
tasks: Audit: enumerate components and token usages that fail contrast tests in prod dark theme (Jonah)
Experiment: prototype delta blend algorithm in Figma + small JS playground (Aisha)
Design: produce token mapping matrix and component override mockups for buttons, tables, charts (Aisha)
Dev sync: review runtime perf impact and kernel for token remap during theme switch (Infra/Runtime)
Docs: write migration notes and sample code snippets for Console theming SDK (Docs)
QA: automated contrast checks and visual regression snapshots for affected routes (QA)
Rollout: feature flag behind console-theme-v2; staged rollout to beta orgs (PM/Eng)
Post-mortem: collect telemetry on theme switch errors and user-reported regressions (Support)
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha: Created initial ticket after running a heuristic audit on dense tables. Attached Figma prototype link and early screenshots. Noted that pure desaturation loses brand identity; proposing a chroma-preserving approach.

2026-03-02 - Jonah: Ran automated contrast tests across 12 components. Found 37 failures (mostly table rows + ghost buttons). Added list to the audit doc. Eng pairing requested to validate runtime cost for HSLuv transforms.

2026-03-04 - Design review: Team prefers delta-blend + perceptual lightness clamp rather than hard inversion. Decided to preserve hue first, then adjust lightness and chroma to meet contrast thresholds. Action: Aisha to build JS prototype and share perceptual examples.
2026-03-07 - PM (Lina): Customer impact flag: medium. Several enterprise customers asked for better dark theme readability. Recommend prioritizing primary buttons and table rows in first rollout.

2026-03-09 - Jonah: Prototype JS playground shows token transform adds ~0.7ms on theme switch for 250 tokens. Runtime team suggested precomputing transformed tokens at build-time for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted can compute lazily with caching.

2026-03-10 - Aisha: Updated spec to include component overrides for compact density and edge cases (list items with avatars, inline charts in table cells). Figma file updated: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/chroma-preserve-prototype (internal)
2026-03-10 - Design feedback from Accessibility: need contrast checks for hover and focus outlines; add outlines with increased lightness delta instead of scaling alpha.
